individuals.age_at_diagnosis_original_text: At the age of about 18 months
individuals.clinical_diagnosis_basis: urine analysis revealed an increased amount of GHB, a hallmark of SSADH-D, and the diagnosis of SSADH-D was confirmed by genetic sequencing by a diagnostic company (original genetic diagnosis in 2014)

variants.parental_testing_statement: Cys93Phe is the paternal variant and Asn255Asp the maternal variant; the SNPs His180Tyr and Val90Ala were present in the maternal sequencing results, and further sequence analysis showed His180Tyr in the same maternal allele as Asn255Asp, while Val90Ala resided in the other maternal allele, not inherited by the patient. (Methods section prints '(paternal)' after c.538T>C instead.)
variants.functional_evidence_statement: Patient fibroblasts showed barely detectable SSADH protein and significantly reduced SSADH activity. Cys93Phe was expressed in very low amounts with SSADH activity barely measurable (below 5% of the WT) on transient overexpression in HEK293T ALDH5A1 knockout cells; in stable Flp-In-293 knock-in cells it showed very low protein and only background activity comparable with knockout cells. Arimoclomol, betaine or celastrol did not significantly increase expression or activity (knock-in cells and patient fibroblasts). In silico: loss of hydrogen bonds causing structural impairment.

variants.parental_testing_statement: Cys93Phe is the paternal variant and Asn255Asp the maternal variant; the SNPs His180Tyr and Val90Ala were present in the maternal sequencing results, and further sequence analysis showed His180Tyr in the same maternal allele as Asn255Asp, while Val90Ala resided in the other maternal allele, not inherited by the patient. (Methods section prints '(paternal)' after c.538T>C instead.)
variants.functional_evidence_statement: Asn255Asp alone: very low expression and activity barely measurable (below 5% of WT) on transient overexpression; background activity in stable knock-in cells; recombinant Asn255Asp insoluble in E. coli. Double variant His180Tyr/Asn255Asp (in cis): very low expression and background activity in eukaryotic cells; recombinant protein activity 0.1% (0.09 s^-1) of WT, K_D for NAD+ 33 +/- 13 uM (10-fold higher than WT), altered CD and fluorescence spectra. No significant rescue by arimoclomol, betaine or celastrol. Patient fibroblasts: barely detectable SSADH protein and significantly reduced activity.
variants.pathogenicity_as_stated_by_authors: variant of unknown significance (VUS) at the original diagnosis; pathogenic according to this study

variants.parental_testing_statement: Cys93Phe is the paternal variant and Asn255Asp the maternal variant; the SNPs His180Tyr and Val90Ala were present in the maternal sequencing results, and further sequence analysis showed His180Tyr in the same maternal allele as Asn255Asp, while Val90Ala resided in the other maternal allele, not inherited by the patient. (Methods section prints '(paternal)' after c.538T>C instead.)
variants.functional_evidence_statement: Protein amount and activity comparable with WT on transient overexpression and in stable knock-in cells; recombinant His180Tyr retained 83% (54 s^-1) of WT activity, K_D for NAD+ 3.0 +/- 1 uM (WT 2.8 +/- 0.3 uM), tetrameric structure preserved; BindProfX ddG +0.63 kcal/mol. In cis with Asn255Asp (His180Tyr/Asn255Asp) activity 0.1% of WT.
variants.pathogenicity_as_stated_by_authors: benign (per se not pathogenic); deemed without clinical relevance by the original diagnostic company
